fact: Afreximbank says Zimbabwe is processing $5.8 million a month through PAPSS, and that most banks in Southern Africa have joined it.

The Herald reports the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe oversees mobile money by directive: a 2021 directive enforced one line, one wallet, and the February 2026 Monetary Policy Statement directed operators to verify customers by 30 June 2026.
The Financial Gazette reported on 9 October 2026 that CBZ Bank has gone live on the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS).
The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe's 2024 annual report says it licenses, oversees and supervises payment system providers, and reviewed 52 applications from them in 2024.
AfricaNenda's 2024 case study says ZIPIT, Zimswitch's instant payment system, is licensed and regulated by the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe, which mandates mobile money operators to join it.
The RBZ says it has revised licensing and fee rules for money transfer and mobile banking operators.
The article says Zimbabwe's participation in PAPSS is expanding, with local banks processing ZAR 2.41 billion in SADC-RTGS transactions, but gives no PAPSS send-and-receive flows.
